item.description: A comparative report on elite support for outsider incorporation, demographic statecraft, and the political afterlives of immigration regimes.

item.title: Mass and Indiscriminate Immigration as Indirect Corporate Welfare
item.description: A report on when immigration regimes function as state-enabled cost reduction for firms through labor dependence, wage discipline, and public-cost shifting.

item.title: Testing the Hypothesis That Culture Is Parasitic on Unsatisfied Human Needs
item.description: A report on compensatory culture, symbolic substitution, trauma markets, and the conditions under which modern cultural industries feed on unmet needs.

item.title: Intergenerational Extraction in Liberal Democracies
item.description: An analysis of how liberal democratic institutions, through debt and social spending, facilitate intergenerational extraction at the expense of younger and future cohorts.

item.title: Liberalism as Political Domestication
item.description: This report assesses whether liberalism acts as political domestication by substituting thick communal authority with softer but denser forms of behavioral management and administration.

item.title: Liberalism, Equality, and the Leftward Drift Thesis
item.description: An analysis of the thesis that liberalism is inherently unstable and tends to generate pressure for broader equality, assessing whether this leftward drift necessarily culminates in socialism or Marxism.

item.title: Republicans as Moderating Opposition Without a Rival Order
item.description: An evaluation of whether the Republican party primarily acts as a moderating force on Democratic initiatives rather than establishing its own durable institutional alternatives.

item.title: Liberalism, Social Disembedding, and Managed Dependency
item.description: An analysis of the distinct failure mode of liberal political economy, focusing on chronic disembedding, social fragmentation, and managed dependency.

item.title: American Conservatism and the Liberal-Revolutionary Founding
item.description: This report formalizes and tests the claim that American conservatism is intellectually unstable because the United States was founded not as a traditional conservative order, but as a modern liberal-republican revolution. The evidence supports a qualified version of the critique: the founding is liberal and revolutionary at the level of first principles, but more conservative at the level of institutional engineering and social practice.

item.title: Formalizing the Connection Between Modern Progressive Politics and Marxism
item.description: This report argues that modern progressive politics is a mediated descendant of Marxist and Marx-adjacent socialist traditions. The connection is formalizable through genealogical inheritance and selective adaptation, evidenced by institutional continuities in labor organizations, welfare-state policies, and rhetorical frameworks surrounding class power, redistribution, and anti-monopoly politics.

item.title: Puritan Moral Psychology and the Genealogy of American Progressivism
item.description: This report argues that American progressivism is best understood as a partly secularized continuation of a moral-political repertoire established by Puritan New England.

item.title: A History of Quantitative Finance
item.description: A historical and conceptual survey of quantitative finance, from early probability models through modern algorithmic and machine-learning-driven trading.

item.title: Cesar Chavez After the Allegations
item.description: An analytical report on how the 2026 allegations against Cesar Chavez altered the public record, civic commemorations, and historical interpretation of his legacy.

item.title: Fallen Aristocracy
item.description: A comparative inquiry into whether displaced nobles and demoted hereditary elites have outsized influence on major historical transitions.

item.title: History of Business Accounting – A Comprehensive Review
item.description: A historical survey of accounting as a business practice, profession, and regulatory system from antiquity to the present.

item.title: How LLMs Challenge Chomskyan Assumptions
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) have challenged fundamental pillars of Chomskyan linguistics, such as Universal Grammar and the Poverty of the Stimulus, by demonstrating that complex syntax can be induced from distributional statistics alone. This report audits the empirical successes of models like GPT-4 against classic generative assumptions, analyzes the methodological divide between engineering-driven prediction and theory-driven explanation, and reviews the combative scholarly reactions within the linguistics and AI communities.

item.title: Structure and Layout of the Cryptocurrency Ecosystem

item.title: The Economy of Non-Bitcoin Cryptocurrencies
item.description: An analytical overview of altcoin market structure, valuation, manipulation risk, and the economic roles of non-Bitcoin crypto sectors.

item.title: The Yankee Left: Managerial Elites and Moralizing Rule
item.description: This report examines the so-called “Yankee-left” – broadly identified with Northeastern U.S. liberal elites – as a managerial, prestige-driven, moralizing ruling formation. It argues that a class of highly educated professionals and bureaucrats has come to dominate culture and politics through technocratic expertise, symbolic status rituals, and a moralistic discourse.

item.description: A long-form history of linear algebra, from elimination and determinants to vector spaces, matrices, eigenvalues, and the computational era.

item.description: A data-driven overview of the current U.S. tax structure across federal, state, and local levels, with emphasis on rates, revenue composition, incidence, and compliance.

item.description: A practical guide to the hierarchy and interaction of legal authorities in the United States, from constitutions and statutes to regulations, treaties, and common law.

item.description: A long-form history of functional analysis: Banach and Hilbert spaces, operators, duality, distributions, and the concrete analytic problems that produced them.

item.title: A Comprehensive History of Type Theory (1900s--Present)
item.description: A comprehensive history of type theory (1900s to the present), tracing its mathematical origins, its integration into programming languages, and its modern role in proof assistants and verified software/hardware.

item.title: A Social History of "Operators" in Mathematics
item.description: A social history of the mathematical “operator”: how actions like differentiation became objects you can manipulate, classify, and build theories around—shaped by notation, education, disciplinary disputes, and the demands of physics and engineering.

item.title: Ad Hoc "Maulerian School of Film Criticism"
item.description: A structured, neutral reconstruction of MauLer’s implicit critical framework—an “ad hoc Maulerian School”—centered on internal narrative logic, canon consistency, and evidence-first argumentation in long-form YouTube criticism.

item.title: Adolf Hitler's Ideology from Origins to Demise (1907--1945)
item.description: An analytical timeline-style essay on the formation, core components, and historical continuity of Adolf Hitler’s ideology from 1907 to 1945.

item.title: Category Theory: Origins, Invention, and Early Reception (1935-1965)
item.description: A historically grounded overview of category theory’s origins (1935–1965), from the foundations crisis and structuralism to Eilenberg–Mac Lane’s definitions and later expansion via Grothendieck and Lawvere.

item.title: Chartists & Radical Republicans, 1840‑1865: Franchise, Socialism, and the Limits of Alliance
item.description: Chartism and Radical Republicanism compared: franchise politics, land reform, religion, and the contested boundary between democratic reform and “socialism” in the mid-19th-century Atlantic world.

item.title: Christian Socialism in Mid-Victorian Britain
item.description: A research note on mid-Victorian Anglican “Christian Socialism,” focusing on F. D. Maurice and Charles Kingsley, their theological rationale, key texts, and practical experiments in co-operation and adult education.

item.title: Co-opting the Left: U.S. Liberal Institutions and Deradicalization (1945--Present)
item.description: How U.S. liberal institutions have repeatedly absorbed and deradicalized left-wing movements since 1945—through concessions, professionalization, narrative control, and selective inclusion paired with repression—illustrated with cross-era case studies.

item.title: Complex Analysis as a Universal Canvas (Euler to Today): A Research Report
item.description: A research report arguing that complex analysis functions as a universal “canvas”: by reformulating problems in the complex plane and applying holomorphic rigidity and integral identities, one can solve and unify problems across number theory, geometry, PDEs, physics, probability, and combinatorics.

item.title: Comprehensive Marxist Literature (1840--2025): An Annotated Bibliography and Research Guide
item.description: An annotated research guide and reading list of Marxist literature (primary and secondary) from 1840 to 2025, arranged to track both historical development and major thematic currents.

item.title: Conservation of Radicalism and Asymmetric Co-optability
item.description: A complex-plane model of co-optation, class-to-culture substitution, and the asymmetric co-optability of left vs right radicalism.

item.title: Evolution of Marxism
item.description: How Marxism changed from Marx and Engels through Lenin, Stalin, Mao, Western Marxism, Eurocommunism, and post-1989 revivals—plus a timeline from 1848 to 2026.

item.title: From Dirt Track to Durable Highway -- Engineering, Material Science & Historic Precedent
item.description: How to turn a dirt track into a long-lasting highway: subgrade, base, drainage, asphalt or concrete, construction QC, and maintenance, with historical engineering lessons.

item.title: Gender and GAHT
item.description: An evidence-oriented, non-prescriptive report on GAHT in AMAB feminizing care: expected physiologic changes, risks and benefits, timing (early vs late initiation), monitoring themes, and key knowledge gaps.

item.title: HasanAbi as a Platform-Native Political Brand
item.description: A mixed-method profile of Hasan “HasanAbi” Piker: career arc, popularity mechanics, audience formation, controversy/moderation dynamics, and forward-looking platform risk.

item.title: History of HTML (1990--2025)
item.description: A detailed history of HTML (1990–2025): standards bodies, browser wars, XHTML, HTML5, parsing, semantics, accessibility, and modern web platform practice.

item.title: History of Neural Networks in Computing (1940s--2026)
item.description: A detailed timeline and conceptual history of neural networks in computing (1940s-2026), connecting major mathematical ideas, hardware shifts, and institutional ‘AI cycles’.

item.title: Imagining the Imaginary: A Cultural-Intellectual History of the Complex Plane (1748--2025)
item.description: A cultural-intellectual history of the complex plane (1748–2025): from Euler’s symbolic i to Argand diagrams, modern physics, computation, and the aesthetics of fractals.

item.title: Inventing Socialism
item.description: A compact research note on the earliest documented uses of “socialism/socialist” in Britain and France (1820-1840), with mini-profiles and comparative analysis of Owenites, Saint-Simonians, Fourierists, and Cabet’s Icarians.

item.title: Jewish Political Activism in the United States (1880--2025)
item.description: Historical synthesis of Jewish American political activism (1880–2025): labor unions, civil rights, foreign policy and Israel debates, organizational density, and modern digital-era advocacy—plus how myths of “Jewish influence” diverge from measurable channels.

item.title: Kern County and the Cannabis Legal Environment
item.description: A practical legal and compliance overview of cannabis cultivation as it relates to (1) continuing federal prohibition under the Controlled Substances Act, (2) California’s statewide licensing regime administered by the Department of Cannabis Control (DCC), and (3) local control in Kern County and its cities. The article summarizes key constraints that shape feasibility - including Schedule I status, 280E tax treatment, banking friction, licensing categories, local authorization prerequisites, track-and-trace (METRC) obligations, security and recordkeeping rules, CEQA and environmental compliance, and enforcement exposure - with special emphasis on Kern County’s local prohibition of commercial activity and the limited, city-specific exceptions elsewhere in the county.

item.title: Land-Rooted Regional Ethnocultures, Elite Cultural Standardization, and Persistent Right Dissidence
item.description: A theory-driven synthesis on land-rooted rural ethnocultures and the rise of persistent right dissidence under elite cultural standardization, with operational definitions, competing frameworks, and testable implications.

item.title: Male Suicide in the United States (2000--Present)
item.description: A comprehensive graduate-level synthesis of U.S. male suicide trends since 2000, integrating mortality data, demographic disparities, risk/protective factors, policy context, intervention evidence, case studies, and projections to 2030.

item.title: Marx and Engels: Scientific Socialism and the Communist Manifesto
item.description: How Marx and Engels distinguished “scientific socialism” from utopian and reformist socialisms, using the Communist Manifesto, early correspondence, and mid-19th-century press reception.

item.title: Mutualism: Markets Without Capitalism
item.description: A historical and conceptual study of Proudhon’s mutualism: property vs possession, the cost principle, mutual banking, and its relationship to cooperative experiments.

item.title: Number Theory from Euler to Today (Europe & the United States): A Research Report
item.description: A research-report style history of number theory from Euler to the present, tracing the interplay of algebra, analysis, geometry, probability, and computation, and highlighting key results from quadratic reciprocity and Dirichlet’s theorem through modern cryptography-adjacent and “structure vs randomness” perspectives.

item.title: Objectivity vs. Subjectivity: Philosophical Debate and Implications
item.description: A long-form report mapping the philosophical and practical tensions between objectivity and subjectivity—historically and across disciplines (science, social science, journalism, law, aesthetics, and AI)—with an emphasis on intersubjective procedures as the real engine of reliable knowledge.

item.title: Taylor Lorenz: Controversy and Media Ethics (Annotated Bibliography)

item.title: The Formal and Informal History of JavaScript (1995--2025)

item.title: The History and Impact of Homological Algebra
item.description: A narrative history of homological algebra and why its tools (complexes, exact sequences, derived functors, spectral sequences, and derived categories) became foundational across topology, algebra, geometry, and number theory.

item.title: The Matrix as Cultural Technology: A Mythical & Social History
item.description: A mythical and social history of matrices as a cultural technology—how matrix thinking scaled science, industry, and computation, and why “the Matrix” became a modern metaphor for control, networks, and simulation.

item.title: The Semantics of "Analysis" in Mathematics (Newton → Present, Europe & the United States)

item.description: A non-technical field guide to how the worldwide chip industry works: design, fabs, packaging/test, market structure, cycles, bottlenecks, and geopolitics.
